programs.title: Agents Work, People Decide: A Union Workshop on DAO Governance
outcomes: Explain the 'agents operate; people govern' division of labor and the six human-reserved actions
Map a DAO decision cycle from evidence to human final vote
Assess how agent-managed coordination affects worker voice and job design
Draft a worker-friendly governance clause for a DAO charter

sessions.activity: Read the Donatello DAO mission and charter; identify reserved-for-humans actions and discuss why final votes, treasury and appointments stay with people.
Practice Evidence Monitor-style summarizing: teams summarize a sample research brief and compare notes on bias and sourcing.
Role-play a proposal cycle: an agent-drafted proposal is debated, amended and decided by a human vote; debrief on worker representation.
Simulate Task Router coordination of working groups between decision cycles; discuss task allocation fairness.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized workshop feedback: which governance concepts were hardest to grasp, and role-play voting patterns (no names, no employer identifiers).
programs.consent: Participants sign a plain-language consent form before the session; data is optional, anonymized, and any participant may opt out without affecting participation.

programs.title: Sculpting Decisions: Civics on a Florentine Hillside
programs.grade_or_level: Middle school (ages 11-14), adaptable to high school
outcomes: Describe what a DAO is and why some decisions are reserved for humans
Connect Florence's history of public art and civic decision-making to modern digital governance
Explain why privacy and consent matter in shared digital systems

sessions.activity: Explore the mission 'AI governed as a public good'; students sort decisions into agent tasks vs. human-only votes.
Teams act as Evidence Monitors: summarize a short article on AI and public benefit, citing sources.
Class debate and vote on a simple proposal (e.g., a school garden fund), mirroring the human final-vote rule.
Students build a simple progress chart tracking their proposal's outcomes, like the Progress Tracker agent.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized class-level results only: vote tallies and which civics concepts needed reteaching; no individual student data.
programs.consent: Written guardian/parent consent is required for all participation and any data contribution; student names are never collected, and guardians may withdraw consent at any time.

programs.title: Evidence to Action: NGO Training in Agent-Assisted Program Design
programs.grade_or_level: Professional development for NGO program staff
outcomes: Use agent-generated evidence summaries to inform program design without ceding decision authority
Design measurable outcomes aligned to a charter mission
Run a proposal cycle with clear human sign-off gates
Apply responsible data-sharing practices with communities

sessions.activity: Workshop on reading and interrogating agent syntheses: source quality, gaps, and when to commission follow-up research.
Draft measurable outcomes for a sample humanitarian program, modeled on the charter's measurable-outcomes zone.
Turn a program idea into an agent-drafted-style proposal, then subject it to structured human review and amendment.
Define indicators and a tracking dashboard; practice monthly progress reviews against charter outcomes.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized program-design artifacts (outcome templates, indicator sets) for a shared learning library; no beneficiary or community data.
programs.consent: Staff consent via organizational agreement; only de-identified templates are shared, and participating NGOs approve anything before it enters the shared library.

programs.title: Governed by Humans: Nonprofit Board Training for Agent-Managed Systems
outcomes: Articulate fiduciary duties when agents draft but humans enact
Identify the six human-reserved actions and design oversight for each
Evaluate a treasury or windfall scenario reserved for human decision
Set privacy and consent policy for community data

sessions.activity: Board-level walkthrough of the mission and the reserved-for-humans list; map each to existing board duties (fiduciary, appointing, amending).
Case study: reviewing an agent-drafted grant proposal; practice amendment, conditions, and the final human vote.
Design oversight of agent task routing: what boards monitor between meetings, what escalates to a vote.
Build a board dashboard tracking charter outcomes; agree on review cadence and escalation triggers.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized governance patterns: oversight checklist adoption rates and common escalation triggers; no organizational or donor identities.
programs.consent: Board members consent individually; shared patterns are aggregated and de-identified, and any organization can exclude its data before publication.
